description: We are LunaForge, a team passionate about space exploration, technology, and innovation. We are building Luna Navigator, a platform to help evaluate lunar landing sites using sunlight, Earth visibility, and communication data. We welcome creative and motivated members skilled in Web Development, AI, flutter, UI/UX, and Astronomy who want to turn ideas into real solutions.
summary: Missions to the Moon's south pole face extreme lighting and communication constraints, and existing tools for checking Sun and Earth positions are often too complicated to use quickly. We developed an intuitive tool that lets mission planners, educators, and the public compare lunar landing sites and dates. For a chosen site and date, the tool shows where the Sun and Earth appear relative to the horizon, so users can quickly judge power generation potential and direct-to-Earth communication windows. It uses NASA LRO data through QuickMap and Moon Trek, and Earth and Sun positions from JPL Horizons. By turning complex data into a simple visual comparison, the tool saves planning time and makes lunar mission planning easier to understand for everyone, including support for future missions such as Artemis III.
details:
What it does:

Our tool lets users choose a lunar landing site and a date, then visualizes the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the horizon. From this, users can quickly assess two things: how much sunlight a site receives (power generation potential) and when Earth is above the horizon (direct-to-Earth communication windows). Users can compare different sites and dates side by side.

Who it is for:

Mission planners who need fast comparisons, educators who want to explain lunar lighting and communication, and the public who want to understand how lunar missions are planned.

How it works:

We used NASA QuickMap and Moon Trek for terrain and illumination information, and JPL Horizons for the positions of the Sun and Earth. We also used mission information from the Canadian Space Agency's Moon Exploration resources, NASA's Artemis III pages, and Ridgelight for context. Sun and Earth positions are shown relative to the local horizon so that results are easy to read at a glance.

Benefits and intended impact:

Existing tools for this task have complicated interfaces that make it hard to evaluate critical information efficiently. Our tool simplifies this process, helping teams compare sites faster and helping non-experts understand why the Moon's south pole is both attractive and challenging.

Tools and resources:

NASA QuickMap, NASA Moon Trek, JPL Horizons, Canadian Space Agency Moon Exploration resources, NASA Artemis III mission information, and Ridgelight.

Creativity:

We combine light and communication into one simple visual comparison, instead of using separate complicated tools. This makes the information clear for both experts and beginners.

Factors our team considered:

Power availability, temperature extremes, Earth visibility, terrain blocking the horizon, and the need for relay satellites. We also considered ease of use for people with no technical background.
